title: Introduction To Large Animal Nursing
description: Introduction to principles of husbandry and veterinary nursing care of common domestic large animal species. The economics of production medicine will be stressed. Builds on foundational knowledge in anatomy and physiology to understand common diseases related to husbandry. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Describe proper restraint and handling of the horse, the cow, the sheep/goat, and the pig.
List and explain the clinical significance and nursing care for medical conditions and diseases of a horse, cow and small ruminant.
objectives: Identify breeds of horses, cattle, sheep, goats, and swine, and discuss breed-associated uses.
Describe housing and husbandry practices for horses, dairy cattle, beef cattle, swine, sheep, and goats.
Explain feeding and nutritional requirements of horses and ruminants.
Discuss the common diseases of horses, cattle, sheep, and goats, and identify core vaccinations for each species.
Identify the gastrointestinal parasites of horses and anthelmintic products used.
Explain the veterinary technician's role in large animal clinical practice.
content: Common diseases of horses, cattle, sheep, swine, and goats
Select common diseases of livestock and horses
Common equine and ruminant gastrointestinal parasites
Veterinary technician's role in large animal clinical practice
